stories.title: RETS Associates Survey of Financial Analysts Highlights Evolving Workforce
stories.excerpt: The 2026 RETS Associates Financial Analyst Survey reveals a commercial real estate workforce evolving alongside rising compensation, expanding AI adoption and changing career expectations. Now in its 15th year, the survey highlights a generation of analysts earning more, strengthening their financial expertise, and increasingly incorporating AI into their daily work. Yet career mobility remains high, with nearly two-thirds pursuing new opportunities and professional growth emerging as their biggest concern. Average base salary reached $126,890 in 2026, up 7.9% from 2025. “Compensation is the headline this year,” said Kent Elliott, principal of RETS Associates. “Firms are paying more to keep experienced talent, and analysts who keep growing are being rewarded for it.” Sixty-three percent of survey respondents have pursued a new role, down slightly from 66% in 2025. Growth potential and compensation were the top reasons for looking. New York, Orange County, Los Angeles and the Bay Area were the top relocation destinations. Arguably the biggest change from last year is in AI adoption. In 2026, 33% of respondents said AI is actively transforming their work, while another 40% reported a meaningful impact. Last year, only 3% reported a significant impact. The post RETS Associates Survey of Financial Analysts Highlights Evolving Workforce appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: RETS analyst base salary rose 7.9% to $126,890 in 2026; firms competing for experienced talent.
63% of respondents pursued new roles; NY, Orange County, LA, Bay Area top relocation targets.
AI adoption surged: 33% report active transformation, 40% meaningful impact vs. 3% significant in 2025.
stories.summary: The 2026 RETS Associates survey shows CRE analyst compensation climbing 7.9% year-over-year to $126,890, driven by competition for experienced talent. Nearly two-thirds of analysts pursued new opportunities, with growth and pay as top drivers; New York, Orange County, Los Angeles, and the Bay Area emerged as prime relocation destinations. AI adoption accelerated dramatically, with 73% now reporting active or meaningful impact on daily work versus just 3% in 2025.
stories.impact: Rising analyst compensation and geographic clustering in superstar markets (NY, LA, Bay Area) signal tightening labor costs for development teams' in-house and consultant-led underwriting functions. High turnover and AI acceleration will pressure multifamily firms to invest in tech infrastructure and talent retention, raising operational overhead in competitive markets.

stories.title: Simone Retains All Original Tenants at 1200 Waters in the Bronx
stories.excerpt: Simone Development Companies has completed an 8,000-square-foot lease renewal with VNS Health (VNS), formerly the Visiting Nurse Service of New York, for its Bronx regional office at 1200 Waters Pl. The agreement completes a full sweep of long-term recommitments from all three original tenants that joined the building when the Hutchinson Metro Center first opened in 2003. VNS Health joins Mercy University and University Diagnostic Medical Imaging in recently extending their tenancies at 1200 Waters Place. Today, the building serves as a central anchor within the 95%-occupied campus. Simone Development was represented by its in-house leasing and legal teams, while Peter Trivelas and Tara Stacom of Cushman & Wakefield represented VNS Health. Current availability at 1200 Waters Place includes individual suites from 1,186 to 6,737 square feet, alongside a 74,250-square-foot contiguous block. “When we launched 1200 Waters Place nearly 25 years ago, VNS Health and our inaugural tenants shared a bold vision for what the Bronx could become,” said Joe Simone, president of Simone Development Companies. “Their early commitment helped us transform underutilized land into the thriving, 42-acre Hutchinson Metro Center—a regional destination that now welcomes over 13,000 workforce professionals, patients, and visitors daily.” The post Simone Retains All Original Tenants at 1200 Waters in the Bronx appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: VNS Health renewed 8,000 SF at 1200 Waters Place in the Bronx; tenant since 2003.
All three original tenants (VNS, Mercy University, UMDI) have recommitted to 25-year-old building.
Hutchinson Metro Center campus now 95% occupied; 74,250 SF contiguous block remains available.
stories.summary: Simone Development Companies secured a long-term lease renewal from VNS Health (formerly Visiting Nurse Service of New York) for 8,000 square feet of regional office space at 1200 Waters Place in the Bronx. The deal completes full recommitment from all three original tenants at the building since its 2003 opening. The 433,000-square-foot property at Hutchinson Metro Center now stands 95% occupied with select suites and a large contiguous block available.
stories.impact: Strong tenant retention and 95% occupancy at a 22-year-old mixed-use campus in the Bronx validates long-term demand for anchored healthcare/institutional office in the outer boroughs. This signals sustained viability of Bronx submarkets for multifamily mixed-use development adjacent to established employment clusters, particularly near healthcare tenancy.

stories.title: Newmark’s Sean Crosby on Retail’s Post-Pandemic Rise
stories.excerpt: At Connect Retail West 2026, scheduled for Nov. 17 in Los Angeles, panelists in the “Capital Flows, Transactions, and Valuation Trends in Western Retail” will discuss how evolving tenant demand, leasing trends, and asset positioning are influencing transactions and shaping the next wave of retail investment. For Sean Crosby, managing director and EVP at Newmark, the focus will be on valuations, a specialty he has pursued for the past 25 years. Here, he provides Connect CRE with a run-up to the discussion. Q: It’s been an interesting half-decade since the depths of the pandemic, when brick-and-mortar retail faced an uncertain long-term outlook. From a valuation standpoint, what factors have led to the sector’s current status as one of the strongest property sectors? A: I think during the pandemic, the human population got a taste of what it felt like to be indavertently “incarcerated” for a significant period of time and got a dose of reality on how much they/we need social interaction as a species. Once we emerged from the pandemic period, most people were starving for such activity. they were done with solely Amazon or DoorDash drop-offs. As such, this created more opportunities for retailers and restaurant as experiential/entertainment tenants. From an investment standpoint, the decline in the office sector (which has yet to really recover from COVID and not sure to what degree it does; other than submarket-specific niches) has attracted more interest and capital to retail investment and hence a more competitive buyer bidding environment leasing to lower cap rates and higher pricing for many good quality assets. Q: Within the universe of Southern California retail, what sectors have proven to be the most resilient post-pandemic, and where do you see ongoing challenges? A: The good quality lifestyle centers with strong draws, e.g., theaters, restaurants, etc. as well as good quality grocery-anchored centers, are the big resiliency winners. H
bullets: Retail sector rebounding post-pandemic as consumer demand for experiential activity revived.
Sean Crosby (Newmark EVP, 25-year valuation specialist) keynoting Connect Retail West Nov. 17 in LA.
Tenant demand, leasing trends, asset positioning reshaping next wave of retail investment.
stories.summary: Panelists at Connect Retail West 2026 (November 17 in Los Angeles) will discuss how evolving tenant demand and valuation trends are reshaping retail investment. Sean Crosby, managing director and EVP at Newmark with 25 years in valuations, notes that post-pandemic consumer demand for social interaction and experiential retail has reversed the sector's pandemic-era decline, creating new opportunities for retailers and restaurants seeking brick-and-mortar presence.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, retail revitalization in mixed-use corridors (particularly Western markets) can enhance ground-floor viability and NOI for apartment communities, potentially improving development feasibility in value-add or transit-oriented projects with retail components.

stories.title: Class A Res Community in Mesa, AZ Refinanced with $92M Loan
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged a $92.1 million refinancing for Atlas Mesa, a 394-unit, Class A multifamily community in Mesa, Arizona. The property, delivered in 2025, is owned by a venture between The Dinerstein Companies and PCCP, LLC. Located at 5818 E Baseline Road, just west of S. Sunview in one of Mesa’s fastest-growing corridors, Atlas Mesa provides direct access to major employment centers along with exceptional amenities. The four-story property offers a mix of studio, one-, two- and three-bedroom layouts with an average unit size of 991 square feet. Brad Miner, Cameron Cureton, Drew Lydon, Justin Savoie, Andrew Pappas and Jack Kurschat with JLL Capital Markets Debt Advisory team originated the loan. It was funded through QuadReal Property Group, led by Brandon Bachner out of the firm’s Los Angeles office. “This transaction reflects strong lender confidence in both the asset’s quality and the sponsors’ proven ability to execute rapid lease-up in one of the Southwest’s highest-growth rental markets,” said Miner. The post Class A Res Community in Mesa, AZ Refinanced with $92M Loan appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Atlas Mesa (394-unit Class A, delivered 2025) refinanced at $92.1M in Mesa, Arizona.
JLL arranged financing through QuadReal; lenders cite strong confidence in asset quality and sponsor execution.
Property located in one of Mesa's fastest-growing corridors near major employment centers.
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged a $92.1 million refinancing for Atlas Mesa, a 394-unit Class A multifamily community delivered in 2025 in Mesa, Arizona. The property, owned by a Dinerstein Companies and PCCP venture, features a mix of studio through three-bedroom units with 991-square-foot average size. The loan was funded through QuadReal Property Group, reflecting strong lender confidence in both asset quality and sponsor execution capabilities in the Southwest's high-growth rental market.
stories.impact: Early-cycle refinancing (just 1 year after delivery) of a new supply asset in Mesa signals lender appetite for quality multifamily in growing Arizona submarkets and validates rapid lease-up in the Southwest. This supports continued development pipeline investment in Phoenix-metro markets, though refinancing at comparable leverage and rates depends on sustained employment growth and in-migration demand in East Mesa corridors.

stories.title: Bozzuto, Kimco Close on JV for Wilton Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Bozzuto and Kimco Realty have closed on a joint venture to develop a mixed-use community in Wilton, CT. The project will bring 168 apartment residences and approximately 11,000 square feet of ground-floor retail to a 5.62-acre site within the Kimco Wilton Office Campus along River Road, advancing the redevelopment of an existing office property in Fairfield County. The third JV between Bozzuto and Kimco, the development is immediately adjacent to Kimco’s Wilton River Park Shopping Center. The site is also directly across from Schenck’s Island Park and the Norwalk River Valley Trail and approximately a mile from Wilton’s Metro-North train station. “Wilton is our value-creation flywheel in action,” said Conor Flynn, CEO of Kimco Realty. “By unlocking the highest and best use of land we already own, next to our Stop & Shop-anchored Wilton River Park center, we create lasting value and strengthen a grocery-anchored neighborhood shopping center our shoppers rely on every day. Bozzuto’s residential expertise makes them an ideal partner to bring this vision to life.” The post Bozzuto, Kimco Close on JV for Wilton Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Bozzuto and Kimco closed JV for 168-unit mixed-use in Wilton, CT on 5.62-acre site.
Project on Kimco-owned land within office campus; 11,000 SF ground-floor retail adjacent to Wilton River Park shopping center.
Site walkable to Metro-North, Schenck's Island Park, Norwalk River Valley Trail.
stories.summary: Bozzuto and Kimco Realty closed on a joint venture to develop a 168-unit apartment community with 11,000 square feet of ground-floor retail on a 5.62-acre Kimco-controlled site in Wilton, Connecticut. Located within the Kimco Wilton Office Campus along River Road, the project advances redevelopment of existing office land and leverages adjacency to Kimco's Stop & Shop-anchored Wilton River Park Shopping Center. The site sits approximately one mile from Wilton's Metro-North train station and is directly across from Schenck's Island Park.
stories.impact: Office-to-residential conversion in a Fairfield County Metro-North town strengthens demand signals for mixed-use, transit-oriented multifamily in suburban Connecticut corridors. Kimco's retail anchoring (grocery-focused) de-risks ground-floor leasing and enhances NOI stability; this playbook is replicable across secondary metros with underutilized office and strong transit access, creating value-creation opportunities for developers with retail partnerships.

stories.title: Can Nithya Raman Break L.A.’s Development Gridlock?
stories.excerpt: Los Angeles City Councilmember and mayoral candidate Nithya Raman speaks to the media. PHOTO: Mario Tama/Getty Images After being sworn in as Los Angeles’s 43rd executive nearly four years ago, Mayor Karen Bass immediately declared a state of emergency, signaling her resolve to tackle the homelessness crisis and marshal the city’s resources to confront this long-standing issue. We don’t yet know what progressive Councilmember and Mayor-elect Nithya Raman will say on the day she officially assumes the role of Mayor on Dec. 14, but it’s certain that acting on housing — and acting fast — will be a key focus. “If I am elected, my first 100 days will be about getting that work underway so that our city can once again build,” Raman said during a speech in October. (Raman’s transition team did not return a request for comment.) In an era where Los Angeles has been riven by ICE raids and slow to recover from devastating wildfires, and after an election where economic issues and accountability were paramount, it may be reductive to say housing is the key issue. But as Los Angeles continues to face a decades-long affordability crisis — as well as a crisis of confidence in city government and the ability to build — housing and real estate issues remain at the forefront. The same week as the election, news broke that Brookfield abandoned its $600 million luxury downtown high-rise, the Beaudry, a massive vote of no-confidence in Downtown Los Angeles highlighting a deep-seated development morass. Policy has long been considered a Raman strength. The 45-year-old urban planner, a graduate of both Harvard and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, has long been championed by pro-housing and YIMBY advocates as a wonk who can get in the weeds. “I’m a planner first and foremost, and a politician as a means to an end,” she told the American Planning Association in 2022. The ambitious housing agenda she laid out on the campaign trail squares with many of the issues voters
bullets: Nithya Raman sworn in as Los Angeles's 44th mayor on Dec. 14, 2025.
Progressive councilmember pledged first 100 days focused on housing and accelerating development.
L.A. zoning and entitlement gridlock is central concern; Raman promised 'our city can once again build.'
stories.summary: Progressive Los Angeles City Councilmember Nithya Raman was elected mayor and will assume office on December 14, 2025. During her campaign, Raman emphasized that her first 100 days would prioritize housing and removing regulatory barriers to development. Her victory signals a policy shift toward loosening zoning and entitlement constraints that have hindered multifamily construction in the city.
stories.impact: Raman's election and explicit commitment to breaking L.A. development gridlock could materially accelerate permitting timelines, reduce soft costs from entitlement delays, and lower risk premium for multifamily projects in Los Angeles. Developers should monitor policy rollouts on zoning reform, expedited review tracks, and density bonuses—potential near-term upside for infill projects in supply-constrained coastal and central LA submarkets.

stories.title: VNS Health Renews 8K-SF Lease at the Bronx’s Hutchinson Metro Center
stories.excerpt: VNS Health, formerly known as the Visiting Nurse Service of New York, has renewed its 8,000-square-foot lease for its regional office at 1200 Waters Place in the Morris Park neighborhood of the Bronx, property owner Simone Development Companies announced Wednesday. The senior care and in-home nursing provider has been a tenant at the mixed-use property since 2003. The 433,000-square-foot 1200 Waters Place is part of Hutchinson Metro Center, a mixed-use campus that features office, retail, medical space and a Marriott hotel. The asking rent and the length of the lease renewal were not disclosed. The average asking rent for office space in the Bronx runs between $25 and $60 per square foot, according to listings on CommercialSearch.com. Peter Trivelas and Tara Stacom from Cushman & Wakefield represented VNS Health in this deal, while Simone Development was represented in-house. C&W did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. “When we launched 1200 Waters Place nearly 25 years ago, VNS Health and our inaugural tenants shared a bold vision for what the Bronx could become,” Joe Simone, president of Simone Development, said in a statement. “Their early commitment helped us transform underutilized land into the thriving, 42-acre Hutchinson Metro Center — a regional destination that now welcomes over 13,000 workforce professionals, patients and visitors daily.” Other tenants at Hutchinson Metro Center include eye health care provider SightMD. It is also home to the Bronx campus of Mercy University. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: VNS Health renewed 8,000 SF office lease at 1200 Waters Place, Bronx; tenant since 2003.
Mixed-use Hutchinson Metro Center features office, retail, medical space, and Marriott hotel.
Office rents in Bronx range $25–60/SF; lease terms and rate not disclosed.
stories.summary: VNS Health (formerly Visiting Nurse Service of New York), a senior care and in-home nursing provider, renewed its 8,000-square-foot regional office lease at 1200 Waters Place in the Morris Park neighborhood of the Bronx. The tenant has occupied the property since its 2003 opening. The 433,000-square-foot property is part of Hutchinson Metro Center, a mixed-use complex that includes office, retail, medical space, and a Marriott hotel. Office rents in the Bronx average $25–$60 per square foot.
stories.impact: Duplicate of article [2]; see that analysis. Long-term healthcare tenant retention validates outer-borough mixed-use campuses as stable demand anchors for multifamily development.

stories.title: Jacob Fulop Files Plans for Two 99-Unit Buildings in East Harlem
stories.excerpt: Developer Jacob Fulop just filed plans for a second 99-unit building in Manhattan’s East Harlem neighborhood. The filing brings the total number of planned apartments for 306 East 101st Street and 307 East 100th Street to 198 units. The two 99-unit projects are likely part of the ongoing trend of using New York State tax programs such as 485-x to avoid paying higher wages for construction workers when developments are 100 units or larger. Plans for the pair of 11-story buildings call for a gym at the top of 306 East 101st Street and 5,757 square feet of outdoor recreation space, according to PincusCo, which first reported the Nov. 2 filing. The targeted development area appears to be community baseball fields and green space at the moment, running directly adjacent to the Metro North Court apartments at 1952 Second Avenue. It’s unclear who owns the land. LIHC Investment Group seems to be the only entity tied to ownership of 306 East 101st Street, as property records show LIHC borrowed money against the property. Fulop has developed five new projects in the city in the past three years, according to PincusCo. He could not be reached for comment. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Jacob Fulop filed plans for second 99-unit building in East Harlem; total 198 units across two sites.
Two 11-story buildings at 306 E 101st St and 307 E 100th St use 485-x tax program to avoid prevailing wage.
Site is community baseball fields/green space; located near Metro-North Court apartments, Schenck's Island Park proximity.
stories.summary: Developer Jacob Fulop filed plans for a second 99-unit building in Manhattan's East Harlem, bringing total planned apartments to 198 units across two sites (306 East 101st Street and 307 East 100th Street). The filing suggests use of New York State's 485-x tax program to avoid prevailing wage requirements triggered by 100-unit-or-larger projects. The 11-story buildings feature a gym and 5,757 square feet of outdoor recreation space; ownership structure remains unclear, though LIHC Investment Group holds mortgage on one parcel.
stories.impact: Strategic use of 485-x tax program to split projects below 100-unit threshold is a cost-containment tactic signaling developer pressure on construction labor costs in East Harlem—a rapidly gentrifying Upper East Side submarket. Rising supply (198 units + existing metro-area pipeline) will test East Harlem rents; developers targeting this area should monitor absorption rates and unit economics, as construction cost savings may be offset by increased competitive leasing pressure.

stories.title: CP Group-Led JV Lands $272M for Mixed-Use Boca Raton Campus
stories.excerpt: A joint venture led by CP Group has secured $271.5 million in financing from a Blackstone affiliate for the acquisition and planned renovation of the 30-Acre Mizner Park complex in Downtown Boca Raton, Fla., property records show. The JV paid $193 million for the 838,840-square-foot Mizner Park, which sits adjacent to the Boca Raton Museum of Art, along North Dixie Highway, near the Brightline station. The property houses 268,391 square feet of office space, 276,461 square feet of retail space and 272 apartments across 293,988 square feet. CP Group originally developed Mizner Park between 1991 and 1999 on land owned by the city. Last week, the Boca Raton-based investor gained control of the asset — with partners Georgetown Company, Acre and StepStone — through ground leases. The transaction breaks down to $113.1 million for the retail component, $46.3 million for the residential component, and $33.5 million for the office component, according to documents filed to Palm Beach County. The previous lessee, Brookfield, gained control of Mizner Park in 2018 through its $9 billion acquisition of General Growth Properties. “Our goal is to bring new energy and investment to this landmark destination while preserving what has made it such an important part of the community and a jewel of the city for generations,” Angelo Bianco, managing partner of CP Group, said in a statement. The surplus in financing from Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies will likely fund the planned renovations, which include upgrades to the building’s facades, landscaping, back-of-house infrastructure, and office common areas. Acre will oversee the multifamily component of Mizner Park, including a renovation. JLL’s Danny Finkle, Matt McCormack and Michael Roukis represented the sellers, while Danny Kaufman, Preston Bacon and Paul Stasaitis, also from JLL, arranged financing. bullets: CP Group-led JV acquired 30-acre Mizner Park (Boca Raton) for $193M; $271.5M total financing from Blackstone affiliate.
Asset includes 272 apartments (293,988 SF), 268,391 SF office, 276,461 SF retail in 838,840 SF complex.
CP Group original developer (1991–1999); now repositioning via ground-lease control with partners Georgetown, Acre, StepStone.
stories.summary: A CP Group-led joint venture (with Georgetown Company, Acre, and StepStone) secured $271.5 million in Blackstone affiliate financing for acquisition and planned renovation of the 30-acre Mizner Park mixed-use complex in Downtown Boca Raton. The JV paid $193 million for the 838,840-square-foot property, which comprises 272 apartments, 268,391 square feet of office, and 276,461 square feet of retail. CP Group originally developed the site between 1991 and 1999; the latest transaction involves ground-lease control.
stories.impact: Large-scale mixed-use repositioning in Downtown Boca Raton near Brightline transit and cultural anchors signals strong capital availability for value-add multifamily redevelopment in South Florida gateway markets. The $271.5M senior financing on a $193M acquisition cost implies favorable debt markets for quality mixed-use assets; developers should view this as validation of Boca Raton's transit-oriented recovery and potential lease-up tailwinds for apartment supply in the submarket.

stories.title: Goodman Capital Leads $31M Condo Inventory Loan on Seattle-Area Resi Tower
stories.excerpt: Create World Real Estate has nabbed $30.6 million of condominium inventory financing for a luxury residential tower east of Seattle, Commercial Observer has learned. Goodman Capital supplied a $25.625 million senior loan secured by the unsold residential units at Mari, a 20-story condo building in Downtown Bellevue, Wash., that opened in fall 2024. JEMM Capital Partners also provided a $4.95 million mezzanine loan as part of the transaction that supports the sponsor through the sale of the remaining condos in the 138-unit property. “Downtown Bellevue has become one of the Pacific Northwest’s most important urban centers, with major employers, shopping and transit close by, and Mari places residents in the middle of it,” Eric Goodman, managing partner at Goodman Capital, said in a statement. Located at 10232 Northeast 10th Street 10 miles east of Downtown Seattle, Mari was designed by MZA Architecture with interiors by B+H. Resident amenities include a sky lounge with a kitchen, a rooftop terrace with grilling stations, a fitness center and a yoga studio. Bellevue-based Create World Real Estate sealed a $95 million construction loan from Madison Realty Capital for the Mari condo tower in October 2021, Commercial Observer first reported at the time. “This transaction reflects our continued focus on financing high-quality assets in dynamic markets alongside experienced sponsors,” Matt Meltsner, partner and head of originations at JEMM Capital Partners, said in a statement. Create World Real Estate did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Mari (138-unit condo tower, Downtown Bellevue) closed $30.6M inventory financing; $25.6M senior + $4.95M mezzanine.
Goodman Capital led senior tranche; JEMM Capital provided mezzanine; building delivered Fall 2024.
Downtown Bellevue positioned as major Pacific Northwest urban center with employers, transit, shopping proximity.
stories.summary: Create World Real Estate secured $30.6 million in condominium inventory financing for Mari, a 138-unit luxury condo tower in Downtown Bellevue, Washington that opened in Fall 2024. Goodman Capital provided a $25.625 million senior loan backed by unsold units, while JEMM Capital Partners supplied a $4.95 million mezzanine tranche to support the sponsor through completion of remaining condo sales. The financing underscores strong capital availability for completed luxury residential product in the Pacific Northwest.
stories.impact: Mezzanine-supported inventory financing for a completed 138-unit condo product in Bellevue signals healthy condo absorption and lender confidence in the Downtown Bellevue market as a Pacific Northwest employment and urban amenity hub. For apartment developers, this validates transit-connected, urban-infill positioning in secondary West Coast metros; conversely, unsold condo inventory at a premium product suggests bifurcated demand (rental vs. for-sale) that may compress rents in comparable multifamily assets nearby.
